title: Affirmative possession with plural owners
summary: Build plural-owner possession statements: owner + on + one thing.
objectives: Build plural-owner possession statements: owner + on + one thing.
Apply the pattern using the supporting forms shown.

sections.title: How the pattern works
paragraphs: Build plural-owner possession statements: owner + on + one thing.
Choose meillä, teillä, and heillä from the intended owner. Put on after the owner, then the noun in its basic singular form.
keyPoints: Build plural-owner possession statements: owner + on + one thing.

steps: First put meillä in the owner position. meillä means “we as the owner”.
Next put on after the owner: “have”.
End with koira (“dog”) in its basic singular form. The order is owner + on + thing.
First put teillä in the owner position. teillä means “you as the owner” for a group.
Next put on after the owner: “have”.
End with kirja (“book”) in its basic singular form. The order is owner + on + thing.
First put heillä in the owner position. heillä means “they as the owner”.
Next put on after the owner: “have”.
End with kissa (“cat”) in its basic singular form. The order is owner + on + thing.
First put teillä in the owner position. teillä means “you as the owner” for a group.
Next put on after the owner: “have”.
End with tyyny (“pillow”) in its basic singular form. The order is owner + on + thing.

commonMistakes: Learn the possessor pronoun as a whole form.
Keep the owner form and the singular thing in their taught positions.

practiceExercises.prompt: Optional practice: Translate “Heillä on pallo.” into English.
practiceExercises.explanation: The -lla/-llä phrase identifies the owner; on stays fixed in this possession pattern.

sentenceExplanation.pattern: possessor + fixed on + one thing in its basic singular form

parts.role: possessor: the person who has the thing
parts.formation: he has the learned possession form heillä; its -lla/-llä ending marks the possessor. Learn this pronoun form as a whole.
Olla means “to be”; possession uses its fixed on form with every owner, including we and they.
pallo stays in its basic singular form: one ball.
